The procurement of medicines shall be carried out through the Government e Marketplace (GeM) Portal in accordance with the prevailing rules, guidelines, and procedures prescribed by the Government from time to time. 2. All bidders participating in the tender process shall mandatorily supply samples of the quoted medicines on the date, time, and venue as mentioned in the bid document or communicated by the purchaser. 3. The samples submitted by the bidders shall be examined, tested, and reviewed by a Committee constituted by the Principal/Competent Authority. 4. The Technical Bid of only those bidders shall be considered responsive and qualified whose submitted samples are found acceptable by the Committee with respect to quality, specifications, packaging, labeling, and other required standards. 5. In case a bidder fails to submit samples within the stipulated time or the submitted samples are rejected by the Committee, the Technical Bid of such bidder shall be liable to be rejected without any further correspondence. 6. The supplied medicines shall conform to the specifications, standards, shelf-life requirements, and quality parameters prescribed in the bid document and applicable statutory provisions. 7. The bidder shall possess all valid licenses, permissions, and registrations required under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act and other applicable laws for manufacture, distribution, and supply of medicines. 8. The purchaser reserves the right to accept or reject any or all bids, wholly or partly, without assigning any reason thereof. 9. Other terms and conditions, eligibility criteria, payment provisions, delivery schedules, penalties, and contractual obligations as applicable and prescribed on the GeM Portal shall form an integral part of this tender/purchase process. .
